key_insight: Long-range interactions let digital-analog quantum neural networks match short-range models on supervised tasks with fewer layers or shorter evolution times.
engineering_relevance: Combining single-qubit gates with long-range analog evolution can reduce circuit resources and classical optimization overhead for hybrid quantum learning.
method: Alternate single-qubit digital operations with analog Ising evolution using power-law interactions.
Study how interaction range, transverse field, and evolution time affect expressibility and trainability.
Benchmark supervised image classification and many-body phase detection, plus unsupervised phase detection.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports supervised resource savings and complementary long- and short-range signatures that jointly reconstruct the phase diagram in unsupervised detection, but provides no numerical metrics.
watch_item: Long-range interactions do not outperform short-range interactions in every unsupervised regime, so benefits depend on the task and operating conditions.
paper_title: Digital-Analog Quantum Neural Network with Long-Range Interactions
